title: session open restores its own Claude's slate
intention: bin/cmd/slate restores the newest slate this Claude wrote and lists every other Claude's newest slate in one line, so no Claude opens on another's work as its own.
how: bin/cmd/slate: under --hook read session_id from stdin; who = claude_identity.who(session_id); _newest_slate filters by ownership; build() adds an OTHER CLAUDES roster.

clauses.claim: with a newer slate by akiendelllinux_cc_0 and an older one by akienasus_cc_0, a session named akienasus_cc_0 restores its own slate
the same banner lists akiendelllinux_cc_0's newest slate in an OTHER CLAUDES block with its host, written_at and id
a session named with no slate of its own reads NO SLATE OF YOURS and is not handed another Claude's slate
a legacy author-'CC' slate whose session equals this session's id counts as this Claude's
with no identity at all (no name, no session) the reader falls back to the newest slate of all and says it could not tell which Claude it is

decisions.text: D1: main(): under --hook, read stdin once (json.loads when stdin is not a tty and non-empty; anything else gives {}) and take session_id; by hand, session_id = $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID. who = claude_identity.who(session_id), sessions dir from $CAIRN_CLAUDE_SESSIONS_DIR as claude_identity already reads.

D2: a slate is mine when its author is who.name or in who.former_names, or its session == who.session (non-empty). _newest_slate(who) returns the newest of mine by the existing key. No name and no session: the old newest-of-all, with the warning 'could not tell which Claude this session is; restored the newest slate of all'. Named but none mine: slate None, banner '!! NO SLATE OF YOURS (<name>): opening cold for this Claude; the other Claudes' slates are listed below'.

D3: OTHER CLAUDES block after the slate header: one line per other author (author not 'CC', not mine), its newest slate written in the last 14 days, sorted newest first: '  <author> @ <host or ?>  <written_at>  <id>'. The SLATE header line shows 'author: <author> @ <host>'.

D4: proof bin/proofs/test_session_open_restores_its_own_claudes_slate.py runs bin/cmd/slate --hook as a subprocess with CAIRN_SLATES_DIR and CAIRN_CLAUDE_SESSIONS_DIR at scratch dirs and the hook JSON on stdin, one tooth per clause, house runner; bin/proofs/test_slate.py stays green.

D5: bin/proofs/test_slate.py run() harness runs the reader with no Claude identity: CAIRN_CLAUDE_SESSIONS_DIR at an empty dir beside its fixtures, CLAUDE_PID and CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID removed, stdin DEVNULL; so its author-'CC' fixtures keep reading as before. No tooth changes.
